applies_why: The judge is resolving a link collision (D5 vs C5) by saying CR2 G answers the word rows but Isaiah 7:14's sign-sense stays open, which engages K-C's ban on verse-by-verse chain collision.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': I weighed (a) K-C requires comparing the whole chains' support and forbids resolving the link from Isaiah 7:14's isolated open sense against (b) K-C permits a verse-level underdetermination because an open verse decides nothing by itself; I took (a) because the judge's stated ground is the sign's open sense rather than a chain-footing comparison.
why: The judge's stated ground rests on the open sense of Isaiah 7:14 after CR2 G answers the word rows, so it decides the link at the verse level rather than weighing the chains by footing as K-C requires.
